name: When should I choose a small room bump-out over a full living room addition?
description: Choose a bump-out to expand existing floor area by a few feet for seating; choose a full addition when you need an entirely distinct, newly framed living area.

mainEntity.name: When should I choose a small room bump-out over a full living room addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: A bump-out extends an existing wall outward by a few feet to add usable floor area without constructing an entirely separate, fully partitioned room. A full living room addition involves pouring a dedicated foundation, framing new exterior perimeter walls, and constructing an independent or tied-in roofline. Choose a bump-out if you only need room for a larger sofa arrangement, built-in entertainment center, or bay window. Choose a full addition when your household needs an entirely distinct living space, such as an expanded family room, formal den, or guest lounge.
